content:
Introduction

Howdy, partner. I'm Pat. I have nearly a decade of experience producing thoughtful marketing systems and experiences across physical and digital work. After spending most of my career with agencies, Webflow was my first real startup. My first year on the brand team was intentionally exploratory and reactive; in year two, I wanted to be much more deliberate about how I worked, communicated, and supported the team's ambitions.

How to work with me

I can be flexible in how we communicate. For important conversations, or when we're beginning to work together, I prefer calls or video meetings so we can build context and learn each other's communication styles. I respond best to conversations grounded in graphic-design principles and objective measures of success.

My strongest contributions come from focus, storytelling, delivery, problem solving, and coaching. Getting the work done—and doing it right—is hardwired into my process. I like to understand the hierarchy of a problem, make the work concrete, and then share an early round so other perspectives can improve it.

Communication

For short engagements, lightweight Slack or text communication works well as long as project-management and feedback practices remain clear. For longer collaborations, I value higher-bandwidth conversations early, followed by focused time with the materials. Loom is especially useful because it preserves the reasoning behind design decisions while giving collaborators a precise place to respond.

I welcome direct, honest feedback. If a conversation is important, it helps to know that in advance and to receive enough context to prepare. I process feelings and ideas over time, so a clear first conversation gives me the right starting point.

Working style

Focus helps me carry a project to the finish line, but I am learning to keep that focus from becoming hyper-fixation. Storytelling helps me make ideas memorable, while the counterweight is knowing when the simplest answer is the strongest one. Delivery makes me dependable, though it also means practicing more grace around imperfect decisions. Problem solving energizes me, and coaching gives me a way to help other people see and develop their potential.

Team values

I value autonomy and trust, making a difference, and work that contains adventure or challenge. I do my best work when collaborators have ownership of their own processes, when the outcome makes life meaningfully better, and when a project creates room to learn something new.

I am less motivated by authority, recognition, or management for its own sake. I would rather deepen technical and creative skills, help a team find clarity, and contribute to a shared outcome.

Goals for 2023

Keep it simple. Fine-tune collaboration. Manage work anxiety. Refine the habits that came from years in consulting, particularly urgency and authoritative decision-making, when a more open and collaborative approach would serve the team better. Continue designing in public, sharing work earlier, and building a healthier virtual working practice.

Mantras

Design needs to solve a problem. Collaboration creates an opportunity for experimentation. Vulnerability is required for creativity. Action is one of the best ways to eliminate fear. You will always have problems; spend your time solving the ones you like.
